extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, quality reporting staff, compliance officers, and stakeholders preparing PRA comments for the IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Review and comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) on the proposed information collection requirements and burden estimates associated with the IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking, including eCQM/claims-measure adoptions, modifications, removals, and related data files. Focuses on the justification, burden accuracy, and methods CMS uses to estimate costs/hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA solicitation topics (44 U.S.C. 3506(c)(2)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: We are required to provide notice in the Federal Register and solicit public comment before a collection of information requirement is submitted to OMB for review and approval. To fairly evaluate whether an information collection should be approved by OMB, 44 U.S.C. 3506(c)(2)(A) requires that we solicit comment on the following issues: The need for information collection and its usefulness in carrying out the proper functions of our agency; The accuracy of our estimate of the information collection burden; The quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; Recommendations to minimize the information collection burden on the affected public, including automated collection techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address each of the four statutory topics (need/usefulness; accuracy of burden estimate; quality/utility/clarity of information; recommendations to minimize burden). Cite concrete data or alternative collection methods where possible. Reference the cited statute (44 U.S.C. 3506(c)(2)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM reporting requirement (three self-selected + eight mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current policy under OMB control number 0938-1022 requires hospitals to submit data for three self-selected and eight mandatory eCQMs from the eCQM measure set, for a total of 11 eCQMs, for the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing burden or proposing changes, note that CMS uses a fixed-cap reporting structure (total of 11 eCQMs) for the specified reporting period; adding measures to the set does not automatically increase the number hospitals must report unless CMS changes that cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-eCQM information collection burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The currently approved information collection burden per reported eCQM under OMB control number 0938-1022 is 10 minutes (0.167 hours) per hospital per quarter or 40 minutes (0.67 hours) per hospital annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 10 minutes/quarter (0.167 hours) per eCQM per hospital when estimating incremental burden for eCQM reporting unless compelling evidence supports a different time estimate. CMS uses this baseline in its burden arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of new eCQMs does not change burden if within reporting cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Although new eCQMs would be added to the eCQM measure set, hospitals would not be required to report more than a total of 11 eCQMs; therefore, adding measures to the set would not affect the information collection burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating proposed measure adoptions (e.g., Advance Care Planning and Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE), consider whether CMS keeps the reporting cap; if so, burden estimates should reflect substitution within the cap rather than additive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims-based measures adoption uses existing data (no new burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed claims-based measures are calculated using Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and MA encounter data already reported to Medicare under OMB control numbers 0938-1197 and 0938-1152; therefore, adoption of these measures would not result in a change in information collection burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging burden impact, verify that all data elements needed for the measure are already collected under the cited OMB packages; if not, identify missing elements and estimate additional burden. CMS lists specific measures (e.g., multiple 30-day risk-standardized mortality measures and Excess Days in Acute Care measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure modification using existing data (no burden change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications such as adding Medicare Advantage beneficiaries to cohorts and shortening performance periods (e.g., from 3 years to 2 years) would be calculated using data already reported to Medicare, and thus would not result in a change in burden associated with OMB control number 0938-1022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed cohort or period changes require new data extracts or processing beyond current practices; if they do, quantify additional burden. CMS states the specific modifications to Excess Days in Acute Care measures as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of self-selected eCQMs does not change burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing eCQMs that are available for hospitals to self-select (and are not mandatory) would not result in a change in burden associated with OMB control number 0938-1022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between mandatory and optional measures when estimating burden impact. Example removals: VTE Prophylaxis eCQM; Intensive Care Unit VTE Prophylaxis eCQM; Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy eCQM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maternal Morbidity Structural measure reporting and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maternal Morbidity Structural measure requires hospitals to attest 'yes', 'no', or 'not applicable' to a two-part question. CMS proposes to add a sub-question to collect the name of the Statewide and/or National Perinatal Quality Improvement Collaborative Program in which the hospital participates. The currently approved information collection burden is five minutes (0.083 hours) per IPPS hospital annually, and CMS believes this is adequate to cover the proposed sub-question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating this proposal, consider time required to identify/record the program name. CMS expects no change to the currently approved burden; commenters may supply data if they believe the addition requires more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for calculating wage plus benefits for cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses BLS May 2024 Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates median hourly wage for relevant occupations (e.g., medical records specialists SOC 29-2072) and doubles the median hourly wage to account for fringe benefits and overhead (e.g., $27.53 × 2 = $55.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should note that CMS doubles the BLS median wage as a rough adjustment for total labor cost; provide alternative wage or fringe estimates if you argue the multiplier is inaccurate for your setting or occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for extrapolating total burden and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS multiplies per-hospital burden (hours) by the estimated number of reporting hospitals (e.g., ~3,050 IPPS hospitals; 1,500 non-IPPS hospitals; 11 PCHs; 318 LTCHs) to compute total hours, and multiplies total hours by wage-plus-benefits to compute total cost (examples: 6,100 hours × $55.06 = $335,866).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing aggregate impact, verify denominator assumptions (number of hospitals, quarters, affected entities) and per-activity time estimates. Provide alternative population counts or time-per-activity data to support different total burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program proposed adoptions/removals
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to adopt new measures (Advance Care Planning eCQM; Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE eCQM; Excess Days in Acute Care After Hospitalization for Diabetes; five mortality measures) and to remove or modify others (remove three self-selected eCQMs; modify reporting/submission requirements for Maternal Morbidity Structural measure; require mandatory reporting for Malnutrition Care Score and Hospital Harm eCQMs after self-selection period). CMS states it does not anticipate these proposals will affect information collection burden when calculated from existing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether each proposed adoption/modification/removal truly relies entirely on data already collected under existing OMB approvals. If additional data collection or new processing will be required, quantify the incremental burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH QRP penalty for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by section 1886(m)(5)(A)(i) of the Act, an LTCH that does not meet the requirements of the LTCH QRP for a fiscal year will receive a 2-percentage point reduction to its otherwise applicable annual update for that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory program compliance consequence; comments may address the burden or feasibility of meeting LTCH QRP requirements given proposed measure changes and the impact of the penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCH Quality Reporting Program measure adoptions/removals and burden assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For PCHs (11 PCHs), CMS proposes to adopt the Advance Care Planning eCQM and the Malnutrition Care Score eCQM and to remove the COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among HCP measure. CMS assumes 10 minutes (0.167 hours) per eCQM per quarter per PCH (40 minutes annually per eCQM) and uses the same wage-plus-benefits estimate ($55.06/hr) to compute costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When estimating PCH burden, use the 10-minute per-eCQM/quarter baseline unless you provide evidence for different times; account for PCH-specific submission methods (manual entry vs CSV) when assessing potential time savings from removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating burden changes from removal of COVID-19 vaccination measures
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS estimates removal of the COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among HCP measure will reduce burden by 40–45 minutes per month per PCH for data entry (CDC estimates), and removal from LTCH QRP will reduce burden by 1 hour per month per LTCH (12 hours annually). CMS applies occupation-specific wages (e.g., Microbiologist $58.60/hr; Information Technologist $56.50/hr; Administrative Assistant $43.82/hr) and doubles wages for overhead where applicable to estimate costs/savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commenting on these removals, verify typical local workflows (who enters data, whether CSV uploads are used) and provide empirical time-per-entry figures to refine national estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Technology Thresholds File as evaluation input
rubrics_metrics.description: The New Technology Thresholds File contains the cost thresholds by MS-DRG that are generally used to evaluate applications for new technology add-on payments for the fiscal year that follows the fiscal year that is otherwise the subject of the rulemaking. Two versions of this file are created each year to support rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants or commenters on new technology add-on payments should use the threshold values (published in the file associated with the proposed rule) when evaluating the cost criterion for applications and previously approved technologies assigned to proposed new MS-DRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG Relative Weights file (Table 5—MS-DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains a listing of MS-DRGs, MS-DRG narrative descriptions, relative weights, and geometric and arithmetic mean lengths of stay for each fiscal year. Two versions of this file are created each year to support the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders using relative weights for payment impact analysis should consult the MS-DRG relative weights file for the applicable fiscal year (FY 2005–FY 2027 available) and use the provided mean lengths of stay and weights in modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPPS Payment Impact File
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains data used to estimate payments under Medicare's hospital inpatient prospective payment systems for operating and capital-related costs. The data are taken from various sources (Provider-Specific File, HCRIS Cost Report Data, MedPAR Limited Data Sets, prior impact files) and is abstracted from internal files used for impact analysis. Two versions are created each year to support rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this file (FY 1994–FY 2027) to replicate CMS payment-impact calculations; if questioning CMS's impact estimates, reference the specific IPPS Payment Impact File used.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR/BOR File (Before/After Outliers Removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains data used to develop MS-DRG relative weights and includes mean, maximum, minimum, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation statistics by MS-DRG for length of stay and standardized charges. BOR = Before Outliers Removed; AOR = After Outliers Removed. Two versions are created each year to support rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating relative weight calculations or outlier handling, consult both BOR and AOR versions and comment on the statistical outlier treatment if it affects weight calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPS Standardizing File (variables used to standardize charges)
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains information that standardizes the charges used to calculate relative weights to determine payments under the hospital inpatient operating and capital prospective payment systems. Variables include wage index, cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), case-mix index, IME adjustment, disproportionate share, and CBSA. The file supports the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Standardizing File (FY 2027 available) to validate CMS charge standardization steps; comment if differences in wage index or adjustments materially affect payment estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG Relative Weights Cost Centers File
rubrics_metrics.description: This file provides the lines on the cost report and the corresponding revenue codes that CMS used to create the 19 national cost center cost-to-charge ratios (CCRs) used in the relative weight calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts reviewing CCR methodologies should consult this file to trace cost report line items to revenue codes and comment on CCR construction if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program Supplemental File
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program Supplemental File is only available and updated for the final rule, containing the most recent finalized payment adjustment factor components (most recent available in FY 2026 final rule supplemental file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders evaluating readmission adjustment factors should use the latest final-rule supplemental file; CMS indicates the FY 2026 file contains the most recent finalized components relevant to FY 2027 proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Disproportionate Share Hospital (DSH) Supplemental File
rubrics_metrics.description: This file contains information on the calculation of uncompensated care payments for DSH-eligible hospitals as well as supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal hospitals and hospitals in Puerto Rico for FY 2027. Variables include data used to determine a hospital's share of uncompensated care payments and estimated per-claim uncompensated care payment amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this supplemental file to review or challenge CMS's uncompensated care and DSH payment calculations for FY 2027.
